title: Transforming Learning or Empty Promise? A Meta-Analysis of Generative AI in Education
extended_summary:
This paper asks whether generative AI tools such as ChatGPT improve student learning and, importantly, under what conditions they are most effective. The authors conducted a meta-analysis of experimental and quasi-experimental studies published from late 2022 through 2025, focusing on academic achievement outcomes such as test scores, grades, and GPA. Their goal was not just to estimate an overall effect, but also to identify moderators that explain why some implementations work better than others.

The synthesis included studies using GenAI as part of instruction across K–12 and higher education settings, in both STEM and non-STEM subjects. The authors coded study characteristics including educational level, sample size, learning domain, subject area, intervention duration, and the instructional role of GenAI (for example, tutoring, assessment/feedback, or personalized support). The included interventions varied widely, but all compared GenAI-supported learning against traditional instruction without GenAI.

Overall, the meta-analysis found a large positive effect of GenAI on academic achievement. The strongest and most consistent benefits appeared when GenAI was used for assessment and feedback or tutoring, and effects also differed substantially by subject area, with language education showing the largest gains. Educational level, sample size, duration, and STEM versus non-STEM domain did not significantly moderate effects, though descriptive patterns suggested stronger impacts in higher education and in longer interventions. The authors conclude that GenAI can improve learning when it is aligned with formative instructional purposes and the subject matter, but they also caution that publication bias and high between-study heterogeneity limit overgeneralization.
quality_tier_rationale: This is a meta-analysis synthesizing 52 experimental and quasi-experimental studies, which is the strongest evidence tier in the requested framework. It reports pooled effects, heterogeneity, moderator analyses, and publication-bias checks, though the very high I² and evidence of bias warrant some caution.
impact_tier_rationale: The pooled effect on academic achievement is large (g = 1.193), clearly exceeding the threshold for blue impact. Despite variability across contexts, the average effect indicates substantial positive impact on general learning outcomes.

interventions.use_case: Meta-analysis of generative AI tools such as ChatGPT used to support learning through tutoring, feedback, assessment, and personalized guidance across educational settings.

finding.finding_summary: Across 52 experimental and quasi-experimental comparisons (two outlier studies excluded from pooling), GenAI-based instruction produced a large positive effect on academic achievement relative to conventional instruction. The pooled effect was Hedges' g = 1.193 (SE = 0.243, 95% CI [0.716, 1.669], p < 0.001), with substantial heterogeneity (I² = 98.0%, τ² = 2.98).
finding.measure: Academic achievement outcomes such as test scores, grades, and GPA
